history.summary: DUPLICATE of seq 705 ('Shri Govindajee Temple', id shri-govindajee-temple) - the same famous temple; the earlier CSV row mislabeled its town/state as Mairang/Meghalaya, while this row correctly places it at Imphal, Manipur. The Shri Govindajee Temple stands beside the former royal palace in central Imphal and is the principal Vaishnavite shrine of Manipur, the presiding deity of the erstwhile Manipuri kingdom. The twin-domed white shrine houses Govindaji (Krishna) and Radha in the central chamber, with Jagannath-Subhadra-Balabhadra and Krishna-Balarama in adjoining chambers. It is the centre of Manipuri Ras Lila performances and the Kang (Rathayatra) festival.

town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur in northeast India, set in a valley ringed by hills at about 786 m elevation. It is the cultural heart of the Meitei people - home to the Kangla palace ruins, the Ima Keithel women's market, Loktak Lake nearby, and a living Vaishnavite tradition expressed through the Manipuri Ras Lila dance. The city blends its royal past with a vibrant contemporary arts and sports culture.
